notes: The Mega Ring handover. DECIDED BY THE OWNER: the player's NPC counterpart (Dawn if
the player is Lucas, Lucas if the player is Dawn) gives the Mega Ring in Hearthome
City after Fantina, gym 3. This supersedes docs/research/mega-design.md 2.4, which
had proposed Cynthia as the giver; the checkpoint itself (after Fantina,
mega_unlocked_at = badge:relic) is unchanged from that document.
The Mega button is gated on GameState.has_key_stone() AND GameState.mega_unlocked(),
so granting the Key Stone here is what actually turns it on. flag:mega_ring_received
is the story flag: it makes the event idempotent and lets later scripts and the UI
tutorial test for the handover without inspecting the bag.
The lopunnite is the one usable Mega Stone in the world at this moment
(mega-design.md 2.1). Remove that one give-item step if the stone tiering changes.
requiresMapObjects lists the object ids data/maps/hearthome_city.json must declare;
the event addresses positions by object id, never by raw coordinates.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: {player}! There you are!
I just came from the Gym. Fantina told me you beat her.
So... you saw it too, then. Her Gengar.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: The way it changed. That light.
Professor Rowan calls it Mega Evolution. He has been trying to explain it since Veilstone.
That whole city is built on meteorite. One impact, one shower of fragments, scattered right across Sinnoh.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: The big fragments became Mega Stones. A Pokemon holds one and it can answer.
But it cannot answer nothing. Something has to be calling.
That is what this is.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: The Professor had two made. One for me, one for you.
Here. Take it.

steps.speaker: system
lines: {player} received the MEGA RING!
The Key Stone set into the band catches the light and holds it.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: Wear it and your bond does the rest.
In a battle you will see the option. One Pokemon, one time per battle — that is all the stone will give you.
And it has to be holding its own Mega Stone. The right one. They only pair one way.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: Which is the problem. Rowan only had the one spare stone.
Take it. It is for Lopunny — and there are Buneary all through Eterna Forest, so you have no excuse.

steps.speaker: system
lines: {player} received the LOPUNNITE!

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: One more thing, and I am not being dramatic.
Fantina had a stone. The next Leader will have a stone. All of them will, now.
They are not going to hold back on you just because you only just got yours.

steps.speaker: counterpart
lines: {counterpart}: So go and find the rest. Every Leader you beat hands one over.
I will see you at the next Gym. Do not keep me waiting!
